summary_of_bug: RandomStringUtils.random(count, start, end, ...) does not validate the range before delegating to Random.nextInt(end - start). When end <= start, it currently throws a generic IllegalArgumentException like “n must be positive,” which is misleading because it does not identify the invalid start/end arguments. The expected behavior is to throw an IllegalArgumentException whose message explicitly mentions both “start” and “end.”
